module purpose: neorv32_twi is a bus-controlled two-wire serial controller that stores control fields and transmit words from bus_req_i, generates internal transfer timing from clkgen_i, drives twi_sda_o and twi_scl_o through a transfer engine, samples twi_sda_i and twi_scl_i, places received words into an RX FIFO, returns control/status or received data on bus_rsp_o, and raises irq_o when enabled and no transmit work remains.

use-case flows.value: control settings written into the held control register fields enable, prescaler, clock divider, and clock-stretch permission
11-bit transmit command/data word enqueued for execution and then picked up by the engine when idle and ticked
serial bit-timing and phase generation, including optional halt when the sampled clock input stays low while the controller releases SCL
execution of the current transfer word: command selection, SDA/SCL driving, SDA sampling, shift/count update, and receive-word commit
control/status fields or RX data returned on a bus read
interrupt request when the controller is enabled and no transmit work is pending or active
bus response, enable/prescaler/divider, interrupt, timing state, sampled inputs, engine registers, and line outputs forced to their reset values while rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.reasoning: A bus write to the control register stores ctrl.enable from bus_req_i.data at line 136 under the addressed write condition at lines 133-135. The stored bit then controls FIFO clearing when low (line 168), clock generation reset/advance (lines 252-257), phase-generator reset to idle (lines 280-281), engine.state(2) (line 321), irq qualification (line 239), and the exported clock-generator enable output (line 270). Integrity is established because these implemented flows depend on the exact stored enable value; availability is established because the bit is held in ctrl.enable until rewritten or reset to '0' at line 124. The bus readback at line 143 exists, but the transport bus port is excluded from structural reporting.

conceptual assets.concept: Serial clock generation and stretch-handling configuration
conceptual assets.reasoning: Bus writes store ctrl.prsc, ctrl.cdiv, and ctrl.clkstr at lines 137-139. ctrl.prsc selects which clkgen_i bit is used at line 257, ctrl.cdiv is compared against clk_gen.cnt at line 258 to generate clk_gen.tick at lines 259-262, and ctrl.clkstr qualifies the halt decision at line 296 so phase advance at lines 282-283 can be stopped. Integrity is established because wrong settings change the implemented transfer timing and halt behavior. Availability is established for prsc and cdiv because they are held registers reset at lines 125-126 and readable at lines 144-145; clkstr is held after a write and readable at line 146, but this RTL gives it no reset assignment.

conceptual assets.concept: Current transfer command and shift word under execution
conceptual assets.reasoning: The start flow writes an 11-bit transmit word into the TX FIFO at lines 197-198. When the engine is idle and a tick occurs, the next word is consumed for execution: engine.sreg is loaded from fifo.tx_rdata bits and inverted ACK at line 327, and engine.state(1 downto 0) is loaded from the command bits at line 329 under the availability/tick condition at line 328; later engine.state selects the operation at lines 322, 344, 353, 387, and 394, and engine.sreg supplies the transmitted SDA data at line 374. Integrity is established because executing the wrong loaded word changes the serial operation that the module performs; availability is established under the RTL-visible dequeue conditions at lines 199 and 328. The queued word in tx_fifo_inst and the bus transport port are outside the reportable structural set here, so the active engine registers are the module-level references.

conceptual assets.concept: Received transfer word captured from the SDA input
conceptual assets.reasoning: The module converts twi_sda_i at line 408, samples it into io_con.sda_in_ff at line 314, and during transfer state '111' shifts the sampled bit into engine.sreg at lines 377-378. On completion, the captured 9-bit word is presented to the RX FIFO by fifo.rx_wdata <= engine.sreg(0) & engine.sreg(8 downto 1) at line 228 and fifo.rx_we <= engine.done at line 229, with engine.done asserted at line 386. Integrity is established because later delivery of received data depends on that captured word matching the sampled line sequence; availability is established under the implemented sample and completion conditions. RX FIFO storage and the bus read transport are not reportable here, so the in-module references are the input pin, synchronizer, and shift register.

conceptual assets.concept: Driven two-wire line levels on SDA and SCL
conceptual assets.reasoning: The engine process assigns io_con.sda_out and io_con.scl_out for start/stop/data/default behavior at lines 335-337, 341-343, 350-352, 357-359, 366-368, 372-374, and 392-393, and these values leave the entity at lines 406-407. By the module-boundary delivery assumption, external consumers must receive exactly these computed line levels. Availability is established because reset/default drive both outputs high at lines 306-307 and 392-393, and active states update them on clocked phases during operation.

conceptual assets.concept: Active-or-pending-work status of the transmit engine
conceptual assets.reasoning: The readout flow reports busy as engine.busy or fifo.tx_avail at line 154. engine.busy is computed from engine.state at line 401, and fifo.tx_avail is produced by tx_fifo_inst at line 194 and then locally tested to start dequeue at lines 199 and 328 and to suppress irq_o until no pending work remains at line 239. Integrity is established because wrong active/pending status misreports controller activity and changes when the next transfer can start or the interrupt can assert. The transport bus output is excluded, so the structural references are the local busy computation and the locally tested FIFO-availability value.

conceptual assets.concept: Interrupt request that the enabled controller has no transmit work active or queued
conceptual assets.reasoning: irq_generator registers irq_o low on reset at line 237 and otherwise assigns irq_o <= ctrl.enable and (not fifo.tx_avail) and (not engine.busy) at line 239. This is a report flow to other logic, so Integrity is established by the exact condition that defines the event; availability is established because the output is produced each clock under the RTL-visible condition.
